text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Social Affairs Minister Franz Hums plans to raise fees for Austria's public health system.
- NATO-chief Javier Solana, currently visiting Austria, has praised Austria's work for NATO's peace keeping mission in Bosnia.
- While Finance Minister Viktor Klima received more than 17 billion schillings from Bank Austria for Creditanstalt ordinary shares, Creditanstalt's preferred shares fell 9.33 percent on Thursday.
- Economic researcher Bernd Marin says Austria's tourism industry needs greater flexibility in terms of working hours to remain competitive.

- Postal holding finance chief Erich Becker says it is only possible to sell around three billion schillings worth of the government's 19 percent stake in Bank Austria on the bourse when Bank Austria is privatised. The government had planned to float the whole stake worth eight billion schillings this year.
- Construction is seen falling one percent this year, which is expected to fuel a seven percent rise in unemployment in Austria's building industry.
- Insurer Wiener Staedtische will keep its dividends for 1996 at the same level as the previous year. Premium earnings were up nine percent to 17.3 billion schillings in 1996.
DIE PRESSE
- While the price of preferred shares in Creditanstalt is falling, an offer by Bank Austria to buy back all shares is possible.
- The savings banks' union wants to take over the City of Vienna's stake in GiroCredit.
- More than half of Austria's insolvencies were caused either by the machinery and metal industry or services firms. Banks have to carry most of the weight.
- Austria is the fifth largest investor in Russia.
KURIER
- Austria's central bank chief Adolf Wala expects 1997 to be an uneasy year for Europe's currencies.
- Klima plans to round taxes down when the European Union's single currency euro is introduced.

- Wiener Staedtische chief Siegfried Sellitsch sees possibilities for cooperating with Austria's largest insurance holding BARC, which was only recently created by the merger of insurers Bundeslaender and Austria Collegialitaet.
- Bank Austria chief Gerhard Randa seems to be the most likely candidate for chairman of the board of Creditanstalt.
- A motorway fee for trucks is expected to be introduced in mid-1999 at the earliest.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Die Erste savings bank and German Bayern Landesbank are possible candidates to take over GiroCredit.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- It is rumoured that Creditanstalt and Bank Austria preferred shares might be merged.
